CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

19	// mirrorCloneRefRe parses the clone-ref shape `entire repo clone` accepts:
20	// the `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` path of a mirror's clone URL, with or without the
21	// leading slash. owner/repo reuse the GitHub identifier charsets from
22	// parseGitHubURL so the same metacharacter vectors are closed at the boundary
23	// (owner/repo flow unescaped into the synthesised entire:// clone URL).
24	var mirrorCloneRefRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^/?gh/` + gitHubOwnerPat + `/` + gitHubRepoPat + `$`)
25	
26	// mirrorCloneProviderGitHub is the upstream provider the `gh` path token maps to
27	// — the value the control plane records and the list API filters on. Kept local
28	// to the clone path so the provider mapping is self-contained rather than
29	// borrowing a constant named for an unrelated (checkpoint) concern.
30	const mirrorCloneProviderGitHub = "github"
31	
32	// entireCloneURLScheme is the scheme of a full mirror clone URL, which
33	// git-remote-entire resolves directly. Such a URL already names the cluster, so
34	// `repo clone` passes it through to `git clone` untouched.
35	const entireCloneURLScheme = "entire://"
36	
37	// isEntireCloneURL reports whether ref is a full entire:// clone URL (vs. the
38	// `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` shorthand that needs a mirror lookup).
39	func isEntireCloneURL(ref string) bool {
40		return strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(ref), entireCloneURLScheme)
41	}
42	
43	// mirrorCloneURL synthesizes the entire:// clone URL for a GitHub mirror from
44	// its cluster host and owner/repo — the form `git clone` accepts, which the
45	// mirror list API doesn't return. Shared by the mirror table view (mirrorRow)
46	// and `repo clone` so the wire format lives in one place.
47	//
48	// HARDCODED ASSUMPTIONS (revisit if either stops holding):
49	//   - The provider path segment is fixed to "gh". Mirrors are GitHub-only
50	//     today; the list/index API (RepoPlacement) records no provider, so there
51	//     is nothing to key off. If a non-GitHub provider ever lands, this must
52	//     take a provider argument or the URL will lie.
53	//   - This is a client-side RECONSTRUCTION, not the server's canonical URL.
54	//     The list index gives only a cluster slug, so callers resolve slug->host
55	//     (clusterHostBySlug, via a separate ListClusters call) before calling
56	//     this. If /repos ever returns the clone URL (or host+provider) directly,
57	//     drop this synthesis and that extra round-trip.
58	func mirrorCloneURL(host, owner, repo string) string {
59		return fmt.Sprintf("%s%s/gh/%s/%s", entireCloneURLScheme, host, owner, repo)
60	}
61	
62	// parseMirrorCloneRef turns a clone ref like `/gh/entirehq/entire-api` into the
63	// API provider ("github") and the lowercased owner/repo. The `gh` token is the
64	// path provider used in entire:// clone URLs; it maps to the "github" upstream
65	// provider the control plane records.
66	func parseMirrorCloneRef(ref string) (provider, owner, repo string, err error) {
67		m := mirrorCloneRefRe.FindStringSubmatch(strings.TrimSpace(ref))
68		if m == nil {
69			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("expected gh/<owner>/<repo> (leading slash optional), got %q", ref)
70		}
71		owner, repo = strings.ToLower(m[1]), strings.ToLower(m[2])
72		if gitHubDotOnlyRe.MatchString(repo) {
73			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("repo cannot be dot-only: %s", ref)
74		}
75		return mirrorCloneProviderGitHub, owner, repo, nil
76	}

79		// must never be silently ignored. Plugins (above) are exempt — what they

106				// user abort (which would also wrongly break an enclosing loop).
107				// procsignal is the shared source of truth written both by the
108				// handler above and by the keyring interrupt path; the latter

122				// subcommand-level arg mismatch. ExecuteContextC returns the
123				// deepest matched command, which is the one that failed.

131		}

166		}

171	// (130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM), falling back to 130 for a signal that
172	// doesn't carry a numeric value on this platform.

175			return 128 + int(s)

177		return 130
178	}
179	
180	// isPositionalArgError reports whether err looks like a cobra positional-
181	// arg validator failure. cobra's stock validators (ExactArgs, NoArgs,

184	// error paths or in the cli's own errors — so it's a stable, cheap
185	// discriminator without reaching into cobra internals.
186	func isPositionalArgError(err error) bool {
187		return strings.Contains(err.Error(), "arg(s)")
188	}

190	func showSuggestion(cmd *cobra.Command, err error) {

192		fmt.Fprint(cmd.OutOrStderr(), cmd.UsageString())

input.prompt:
Design an implementation plan (no code changes — read-only research + a written plan) for a two-part change to the `entire` CLI. Report file:line references, existing functions to reuse, and a concrete step-by-step plan.

## The bug
`entire repo clone /gh/entirehq/entire-records` printed:
```
resolve mirror placements: security "BearerAuth": security source "BearerAuth": login session for "us.auth.entire.io" (https://us.auth.entire.io) expired; run `entire login` to re-authenticate
```
The friendly inner text comes from `reauthError` in `cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go:139-174` (built by `contextReauthError`), which unwraps to sentinels `tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired` (expired) and `tokenmanager.ErrNotLoggedIn` (no login). The noise prefixes come from `cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go:239` (`resolve mirror placements: %w`) and generated ogen wrappers in `internal/coreapi/oas_client_gen.go` / `oas_security_gen.go` (DO NOT edit generated files).

## Decisions already made (do not revisit)
1. Also OFFER to log in and continue — not just clean the message.
2. Do it as a **clone-specific precondition** (check session BEFORE the mirror lookup; if missing/expired, run `entire login` INLINE in the same process, then continue). Do NOT use a central main.go catch or re-exec.

## Part 1 — clean-message base (all control-plane commands)
`renderCoreError` (`cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go:639-647`) is the single choke point for every control-plane command (org/project/repo/grant/mirror/clone via runCore→runCoreClient at corecmd.go:601-617). It currently only maps RFC-7807 errors via `coreapi.APIError` and passes auth errors through raw. Design a change so that when the error chain contains `tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired` or `auth.ErrNotLoggedIn`, it returns just the clean inner `reauthError.Error()` message (strip the noise). Note: must unwrap to the sentinel/`*reauthError`, NOT string-match the top-level message (two noise layers). Check whether `reauthError` is exported / how to extract its clean message from outside the auth package (it's unexported today; `errors.As` won't work cross-package unless exported — figure out the cleanest option: export a helper in the auth package that takes an error and returns (friendlyMsg string, ok bool), vs re-export the sentinel and reconstruct text). `auth.ErrNotLoggedIn` is already re-exported (cmd/entire/cli/auth/exchange.go:14); `ErrReauthRequired` is NOT re-exported and is matched nowhere outside refresh.go — decide whether to re-export it.

## Part 2 — clone precondition + inline login
In `newRepoCloneCmd` RunE (`cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go:78-180`), before `resolvePullablePlacements`/`runWithCore`, add a precondition that ensures a usable session. Investigate and specify:

a) **How to probe session validity cheaply.** The active-context token provider is built via `auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider` (refresh.go:195). Calling the provider func triggers a refresh and returns either a token or a reauth error (ErrReauthRequired/ErrNotLoggedIn). Determine the cleanest way for the clone command to run this probe for the ACTIVE context (and consider: is there an existing "am I logged in / auth status" helper it should reuse instead? e.g. around `cmd/entire/cli/auth.go`, `authcmd.go`, `entireapi_client.go:48`, `api_client.go:35`). Report what `coreapi.New()` / the `activeCoreClient` seam (corecmd.go:564) actually does and whether the probe can piggyback on client construction.

b) **The `--cluster` path.** With `--cluster`, clone dials a DIFFERENT core/context via `runCoreForCluster`→`clusterCoreClient` (coreapi.NewForCluster). A session precondition there concerns a different context. Decide whether the precondition covers only the active-context path (the reported bug) or also `--cluster`, and how to keep it correct/simple. It's acceptable to scope the precondition to the active-context (no --cluster) path and let the --cluster path rely on the Part 1 clean-message fallback.

c) **Invoking `entire login` in-process.** Find the login command entry point (search for the login cobra command, likely `cmd/entire/cli/login*.go` or `auth/*login*`). Determine how to run it in-process so that AFTER it completes, a freshly-built token provider/client in the SAME process picks up the newly stored token (token store / keychain re-read). Confirm whether the token manager caches anything per-process that would make the continued command still see the old expired state (see refresh.go notes about the manager freezing settings / re-reading the store). Specify how to rebuild the client after login.

d) **Interactive gating + agent-safe fallback.** Only prompt+login when interactive: use `interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` (see CLAUDE.md 'Spawning subprocesses / TTY detection' section). When NOT interactive, the precondition must return the clean Part-1 message (so agents/CI see the hint and a non-zero exit) — never hang on a prompt. The prompt must be accessibility-aware (huh + NewAccessibleForm in the cli package, per CLAUDE.md Accessibility section). Confirm the confirm-prompt pattern used elsewhere in the cli package.

e) **Testing.** Describe unit/command tests: how existing tests fake the core client (the `activeCoreClient`/`clusterCoreClient` seams at corecmd.go:564-570), how to simulate an expired session, and how to assert (i) clean message on non-TTY, (ii) prompt+login+continue on TTY. Reference existing test files for repo clone and corecmd (search `repo_clone_test.go`, `corecmd_test.go`). Follow the repo's t.Parallel / testutil / config-isolation rules.

## Deliverable
A concrete plan: exact files/functions to change, new helper(s) and where they live (respect the import-cycle rules — cli imports auth/coreapi; auth cannot import cli), the reused existing functions with file:line, the precise user-facing messages, and the test plan. Flag any risk or ambiguity you couldn't resolve from the code. Do not write code or modify files.

# Implementation Plan: clean re-auth message + clone inline-login precondition

## How the reported error is actually assembled (verified)

For `entire repo clone /gh/entirehq/entire-records` with an expired session:

1. `resolvePullablePlacements` calls `c.ResolveMirrorPlacements`; the generated client resolves the bearer via `providerSource.BearerAuth` (`internal/coreapi/client.go:180`).
2. That calls the active context's refreshing provider (`auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider`, `refresh.go:195`). On an expired session `mgr.Refresh` returns `tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired`, which `contextReauthError` (`refresh.go:159`) maps to a `*reauthError` whose `.Error()` is the clean `login session for "us.auth.entire.io" (…) expired; run 'entire login'…` and which `Unwrap()`s to the sentinel.
3. ogen's security wrappers wrap that (`%w`), and `resolvePullablePlacements` adds `resolve mirror placements: %w` (`repo_clone.go:239`).
4. The whole chain reaches `renderCoreError` (`corecmd.go:639`) via `runCoreClient` (`corecmd.go:613-614`) — so **Part 1's fix in `renderCoreError` directly cleans the reported message**, because the clone lister already routes through it.

Key fact: the `*reauthError` is preserved intact in the chain (both for `ErrReauthRequired` and, under `providerSource`'s `not logged in — run 'entire login': %w` wrap at `client.go:190`, for `ErrNotLoggedIn`). So a single `errors.As(err, &*reauthError)` finds the clean inner message in every case.

## Part 1 — clean-message base (all control-plane commands)

**New helper (auth package)** — `cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go`, next to `reauthError` (lines 139-174):

```go
// ReauthMessage returns the friendly, context-named re-login message carried by
// a reauthError anywhere in err's chain (expired session or no usable login),
// and ok=false when err is not a re-auth error. It is the cross-package accessor
// for the unexported reauthError: callers in the cli package can't errors.As the
// type themselves, and matching the top-level string is wrong (two noise layers
// wrap it). Both re-auth sentinels surface as a reauthError here, so a single
// check covers ErrReauthRequired and ErrNotLoggedIn.
func ReauthMessage(err error) (string, bool) {
    var re *reauthError
    if errors.As(err, &re) {
        return re.Error(), true
    }
    return "", false
}
```

This is the cleanest of the two options in the brief: it encapsulates the unexported type and both sentinels, so **`ErrReauthRequired` does NOT need to be re-exported** and no text reconstruction is needed. (`errors.As` on an unexported target type is legal because the helper is defined in the same package.)

**Change `renderCoreError`** — `cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go:639-647`. Insert between the `APIError` branch and the raw fallback:

```go
if msg := coreapi.APIError(err); msg != "" {
    return errors.New(msg)
}
if msg, ok := auth.ReauthMessage(err); ok {
    return errors.New(msg)
}
return err
```

`auth` is already imported in corecmd.go (line 17). Returning a plain `errors.New` (not `SilentError`) is correct: `main.go:87-88` prints plain errors, `SilenceUsage` is already set by `runCoreClient` (`corecmd.go:602`), and a `SilentError` would be swallowed.

This automatically fixes every control-plane command (org/project/repo/grant/mirror/clone) since all route through `runCore`→`runCoreClient`→`renderCoreError`. It also serves the `--cluster` clone path (Part 2b) as the fallback.

## Part 2 — clone precondition + inline login

### (a) Cheap session probe — reuse existing exported functions, no new auth helper

The probe reuses the exact resolution path `coreapi.New()` uses. `coreapi.New` (`client.go:35`) → `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()` (`control_plane.go:47`) → builds `ControlPlaneTarget{CoreURL, TokenSource}` where `TokenSource` is the refreshing login provider. Client construction itself does **not** touch the network (the bearer is lazy per-request), so the probe must call `TokenSource(ctx)` explicitly — that triggers `mgr.Refresh` and returns a token or a `*reauthError`. Both `ResolveControlPlaneTarget` and `TokenSource` are already exported, so no new auth API is needed for the probe.

`ResolveControlPlaneTarget` does **not** honor `ENTIRE_TOKEN` (only `coreapi.New` does, via `clientFromEnvToken`), so the precondition must be skipped when `ENTIRE_TOKEN` is set (those runs are non-interactive CI anyway; Part 1 covers them).

There is no better existing "am I logged in" helper to reuse: `resolveStatusTarget` (`auth.go:328`) deliberately *swallows* the reauth error (falls back to `LoginTokenForContext` and reports "not logged in"), so it cannot distinguish expired-refreshable from dead. `RefreshedLoginToken` (`refresh.go:223`) is close but needs a `*contexts.Context` (the active-context lookup is unexported). `ResolveControlPlaneTarget()` + `TokenSource(ctx)` is the clean seam.

### (b) `--cluster` scope decision

Scope the precondition to the **active-context path only** (the reported bug). When `cluster != ""` clone dials a different context via `runCoreForCluster`→`clusterCoreClient`→`coreapi.NewForCluster` (`client.go:58`), whose session is a *different* context resolved by network discovery; probing it cheaply is not worth the complexity. The `--cluster` path relies on the Part 1 clean-message fallback (still an improvement over today). This matches the brief's stated acceptable scope.

### (c) Invoking `entire login` in-process + client rebuild

**Login entry point:** `newLoginCmd()` in `cmd/entire/cli/login.go:73`; its RunE builds `auth.NewClient(...)` and calls `runLoginAuto` (`login.go:219`). After success, `persistLogin`→`auth.RecordLoginContext(token, refresh, true)` (`login.go:330`, sig at `contexts.go:59`) writes contexts.json + keychain and **activates** the new context (`activate=true`).

**Refactor for reuse:** extract the body of `newLoginCmd`'s RunE into a package function so both the command and the clone precondition call it without duplicating the flow-selection logic:

```go
func runLoginToServer(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, server string, insecureHTTPAuth, useDevice bool) error {
    loginServer, err := parseLoginServer(server)
    if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("invalid login server: %w", err) }
    if err := requireSecureLoginServer(loginServer, insecureHTTPAuth); err != nil { return err }
    client := auth.NewClient(loginServer, nil, insecureHTTPAuth)
    startBrowser := func(ctx context.Context) (browserAuthFlow, error) { return client.StartBrowserAuth(ctx) }
    return runLoginAuto(ctx, outW, errW, client, startBrowser, openBrowser, loginFlowFacts{
        useDevice:  useDevice,
        canPrompt:  interactive.CanPromptInteractively(),
        sshSession: isSSHSession(),
    })
}
```

`newLoginCmd`'s RunE becomes a one-line call to it.

**Per-process caching — verified safe.** The precondition runs *before* `runWithCore`. After login, `runWithCore`→`runCore`→`activeCoreClient` (which is `coreapi.New`, `corecmd.go:564`) builds a **brand-new** `*coreapi.Client` with a **brand-new** `tokenmanager.Manager` (`newContextTokenManager`, `refresh.go:116`) that re-reads contexts.json (`activeContext`, `control_plane.go:109`) and the keychain (`contextTokenStore.LoadTokens`, `refresh.go:39`). The manager re-reads its store on `Refresh`, so the freshly-stored token is picked up. The only per-process freeze is the insecure-HTTP setting (`corecmd.go:604-607` note) and the resource-exchange cache — neither affects a login-JWT re-mint from a new manager. **The precondition must not build/keep a client before login; letting `runWithCore` construct it afterward is exactly right.** The discarded probe manager has no cross-instance state.

**Login server to target:** pass the expired context's `target.CoreURL` (the issuer — `newContextTokenManager` keys `Issuer` on `CoreURL`, `refresh.go:124`; the bug shows `https://us.auth.entire.io`) so re-login re-establishes the *same* context. Fall back to `api.DefaultAuthBaseURL` (`= https://us.auth.entire.io`, `api/base_url.go:20`) when there is no active context (bare `ErrNotLoggedIn`, no CoreURL). Thread `insecureHTTPRequested(cmd)` into `insecureHTTPAuth`.

### (d) Interactive gating + agent-safe fallback

Gate on `interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` (`interactive/interactive.go:34`). Non-interactive → return the clean Part-1 message so agents/CI get the hint + non-zero exit and never hang. Use `NewAccessibleForm` (`utils.go:26`) with `huh.NewConfirm`, mirroring `confirmControlPlaneDeletion` (`corecmd.go:130-159`) including the `huh.ErrUserAborted`/`context.Canceled` clean-cancel handling.

```go
func ensureCloneSession(cmd *cobra.Command) error {
    ctx := cmd.Context()
    if _, ok := os.LookupEnv(auth.EnvTokenVar); ok {
        return nil // ENTIRE_TOKEN path: verbatim bearer, Part 1 covers failures
    }
    if insecureHTTPRequested(cmd) {
        auth.EnableInsecureHTTP()
    }
    var probeErr error
    loginServer := api.DefaultAuthBaseURL
    target, err := auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()
    if err != nil {
        probeErr = err // wraps ErrNotLoggedIn (no active context)
    } else {
        loginServer = target.CoreURL
        if _, terr := target.TokenSource(ctx); terr != nil {
            probeErr = terr // *reauthError (expired) or a transient refresh/network error
        }
    }
    if probeErr == nil {
        return nil // session healthy
    }
    msg, isReauth := auth.ReauthMessage(probeErr)
    if !isReauth {
        return probeErr // transient (network) — let normal flow surface it
    }
    if !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
        return errors.New(msg) // clean Part-1 message, non-zero exit, no prompt
    }
    proceed, err := confirmReauthAndLogin(cmd, msg) // NewAccessibleForm confirm
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if !proceed {
        return errors.New(msg)
    }
    return runLoginToServer(ctx, cmd.OutOrStdout(), cmd.ErrOrStderr(), loginServer,
        insecureHTTPRequested(cmd), false)
}
```

Then in RunE:
```go
if cluster == "" {
    if err := ensureCloneSession(cmd); err != nil {
        return err
    }
}
```

Add an `auth` package test for `ReauthMessage` covering: expired sentinel, not-logged-in sentinel, deep-wrapped chain, and a non-reauth error (`ok=false`).

**Part 2 command tests — new `repo_clone_login_test.go`** (NOT parallel; swaps seams). Reuse the `runCoreCmd` pattern (`corecmd_delete_test.go:46`): point `activeCoreClient` at an httptest core (or a stub returning a 401/reauth). To drive the precondition deterministically without the real auth stack, add a package-level seam mirroring `activeCoreClient` — a `probeCloneSession` (or an injectable `resolveControlPlaneTarget`/`loginFunc`) var defaulting to production — so tests can:
  - (i) **non-TTY** (default `go test`, `CanPromptInteractively()==false`): stub the probe to return a `*reauthError`; assert clone exits non-zero with the clean message and **no** login attempt (login stub not called).

# Implementation Plan: clean re-auth message + clone inline-login precondition

## How the reported error is actually assembled (verified)

For `entire repo clone /gh/entirehq/entire-records` with an expired session:

1. `resolvePullablePlacements` calls `c.ResolveMirrorPlacements`; the generated client resolves the bearer via `providerSource.BearerAuth` (`internal/coreapi/client.go:180`).
2. That calls the active context's refreshing provider (`auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider`, `refresh.go:195`). On an expired session `mgr.Refresh` returns `tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired`, which `contextReauthError` (`refresh.go:159`) maps to a `*reauthError` whose `.Error()` is the clean `login session for "us.auth.entire.io" (…) expired; run 'entire login'…` and which `Unwrap()`s to the sentinel.
3. ogen's security wrappers wrap that (`%w`), and `resolvePullablePlacements` adds `resolve mirror placements: %w` (`repo_clone.go:239`).
4. The whole chain reaches `renderCoreError` (`corecmd.go:639`) via `runCoreClient` (`corecmd.go:613-614`) — so **Part 1's fix in `renderCoreError` directly cleans the reported message**, because the clone lister already routes through it.

Key fact: the `*reauthError` is preserved intact in the chain (both for `ErrReauthRequired` and, under `providerSource`'s `not logged in — run 'entire login': %w` wrap at `client.go:190`, for `ErrNotLoggedIn`). So a single `errors.As(err, &*reauthError)` finds the clean inner message in every case.

## Part 1 — clean-message base (all control-plane commands)

**New helper (auth package)** — `cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go`, next to `reauthError` (lines 139-174):

```go
// ReauthMessage returns the friendly, context-named re-login message carried by
// a reauthError anywhere in err's chain (expired session or no usable login),
// and ok=false when err is not a re-auth error. It is the cross-package accessor
// for the unexported reauthError: callers in the cli package can't errors.As the
// type themselves, and matching the top-level string is wrong (two noise layers
// wrap it). Both re-auth sentinels surface as a reauthError here, so a single
// check covers ErrReauthRequired and ErrNotLoggedIn.
func ReauthMessage(err error) (string, bool) {
    var re *reauthError
    if errors.As(err, &re) {
        return re.Error(), true
    }
    return "", false
}
```

This is the cleanest of the two options in the brief: it encapsulates the unexported type and both sentinels, so **`ErrReauthRequired` does NOT need to be re-exported** and no text reconstruction is needed. (`errors.As` on an unexported target type is legal because the helper is defined in the same package.)

**Change `renderCoreError`** — `cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go:639-647`. Insert between the `APIError` branch and the raw fallback:

```go
if msg := coreapi.APIError(err); msg != "" {
    return errors.New(msg)
}
if msg, ok := auth.ReauthMessage(err); ok {
    return errors.New(msg)
}
return err
```

`auth` is already imported in corecmd.go (line 17). Returning a plain `errors.New` (not `SilentError`) is correct: `main.go:87-88` prints plain errors, `SilenceUsage` is already set by `runCoreClient` (`corecmd.go:602`), and a `SilentError` would be swallowed.

This automatically fixes every control-plane command (org/project/repo/grant/mirror/clone) since all route through `runCore`→`runCoreClient`→`renderCoreError`. It also serves the `--cluster` clone path (Part 2b) as the fallback.

### (a) Cheap session probe — reuse existing exported functions, no new auth helper

The probe reuses the exact resolution path `coreapi.New()` uses. `coreapi.New` (`client.go:35`) → `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()` (`control_plane.go:47`) → builds `ControlPlaneTarget{CoreURL, TokenSource}` where `TokenSource` is the refreshing login provider. Client construction itself does **not** touch the network (the bearer is lazy per-request), so the probe must call `TokenSource(ctx)` explicitly — that triggers `mgr.Refresh` and returns a token or a `*reauthError`. Both `ResolveControlPlaneTarget` and `TokenSource` are already exported, so no new auth API is needed for the probe.

func runLoginToServer(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, server string, insecureHTTPAuth, useDevice bool) error {
    loginServer, err := parseLoginServer(server)
    if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("invalid login server: %w", err) }

    ctx := cmd.Context()

# Clean re-auth message + `repo clone` inline-login precondition

## Context

`entire repo clone /gh/entirehq/entire-records` on an expired session prints:

```
resolve mirror placements: security "BearerAuth": security source "BearerAuth": login session for "us.auth.entire.io" (https://us.auth.entire.io) expired; run `entire login` to re-authenticate
```

The actionable inner text is buried under two noise layers: `resolve mirror placements:` (`repo_clone.go:239`) and the generated ogen wrappers `security "BearerAuth": security source "BearerAuth":` (`internal/coreapi/oas_*.go`, not editable). The friendly text originates from `*reauthError` (`auth/refresh.go:139-174`), which is preserved intact in the chain and unwraps to `tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired` / `ErrNotLoggedIn`.

Two improvements (user-approved):
1. **All control-plane commands** — strip the noise, show only the clean re-login hint.
2. **`repo clone`** — treat a usable session as a precondition: if missing/expired and the terminal is interactive, offer to run `entire login` inline and continue the clone in the same process; otherwise fall back to the clean hint.

Not doing: a central main.go catch or re-exec (that's PR #1794's `cli_upgrade_required` shape — deliberately not reused here). This work is unrelated to the current `fix/local-repo-checkpoint-probe` branch and should land as its own PR branched off `main`.

## Part 1 — clean re-auth message (base, fixes every control-plane command)

All control-plane commands funnel errors through `renderCoreError` (`cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go:639`) via `runCore`→`runCoreClient`. It only recognizes RFC-7807 (`coreapi.APIError`) and passes auth errors through raw.

**New accessor in the auth package** — `cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go`, beside `reauthError`:

```go
// ReauthMessage returns the friendly, context-named re-login message carried by
// a *reauthError anywhere in err's chain, ok=false otherwise. Cross-package
// accessor for the unexported type — the cli package can't errors.As it, and
// string-matching the top-level message is wrong (two noise layers wrap it).
func ReauthMessage(err error) (string, bool) {
	var re *reauthError
	if errors.As(err, &re) {
		return re.Error(), true
	}
	return "", false
}
```

Both re-auth sentinels surface as `*reauthError`, so this one check covers expired + not-logged-in; `ErrReauthRequired` need **not** be re-exported.

**Change `renderCoreError`** — insert between the `APIError` branch and the raw fallback:

```go
if msg, ok := auth.ReauthMessage(err); ok {
	return errors.New(msg)
}
```

`auth` is already imported in `corecmd.go`. Return a plain error (not `SilentError`): `main.go:126` prints plain errors, `SilenceUsage` is already set, and a `SilentError` would be swallowed.

This alone fixes the reported clone message (its lister routes through `renderCoreError`) and every org/project/repo/grant/mirror command, plus the `--cluster` clone path.

## Part 2 — `repo clone` inline-login precondition (active-context path only)

Scope: only the `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` shorthand with **no `--cluster`** (the reported bug). The `--cluster` path dials a different context and relies on the Part 1 fallback.

**Reuse the existing probe seam** — no new auth API. `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()` (`auth/control_plane.go:47`) returns `ControlPlaneTarget{CoreURL, TokenSource}`; calling `TokenSource(ctx)` triggers the refresh and returns a token or a `*reauthError`. This is the same path `coreapi.New()` uses; client construction does no network I/O, so the probe must call `TokenSource` explicitly. Skip the precondition when `ENTIRE_TOKEN` is set (`auth.EnvTokenVar`) — that path uses a verbatim bearer and is non-interactive CI; Part 1 covers its failures.

**Extract login for in-process reuse** — refactor `newLoginCmd`'s RunE body (`login.go:82-104`) into a package function `runLoginToServer(ctx, outW, errW, server, insecureHTTPAuth, useDevice bool) error` that runs `parseLoginServer`→`requireSecureLoginServer`→`runLoginAuto`. `newLoginCmd` becomes a one-line caller. Pass the expired context's `target.CoreURL` as the server (it is the issuer, so re-login re-establishes the same context), falling back to `api.DefaultAuthBaseURL` when there is no active context.

**Per-process cache is safe:** the precondition runs *before* `runWithCore`. On success, `runWithCore`→`runCore`→`activeCoreClient` (`coreapi.New`) builds a brand-new client + token manager that re-reads contexts.json and the keychain, so the freshly stored token is picked up. Do **not** build/keep a client before login — let `runWithCore` construct it afterward.

**New `ensureCloneSession(cmd)` in `repo_clone.go`:**
- `ENTIRE_TOKEN` set → return nil.
- Opt into insecure HTTP if `insecureHTTPRequested(cmd)`.

# Ship Changes

Commit current changes, push to remote, and update the PR.

## Step 1: Analyze changes

1. Run `git diff --stat` and `git diff` to understand what changed
2. Run `git status` to see untracked files
3. Run `git log --oneline -3` to match the repo's commit message style

## Step 2: Commit

1. Stage only the relevant changed/untracked files by name (never `git add -A` or `git add .`)
2. Write a concise commit message that focuses on the "why" not the "what"
   - If `draft` is provided, use it as the commit message

3. Commit. If hooks fail, diagnose and fix — do NOT use `--no-verify`

## Step 3: Push

1. Check if the branch tracks a remote: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`
2. If not tracking, push with `-u origin <branch>`
3. If tracking, just `git push`
4. If push is rejected (remote has new commits), pull with rebase first then push

## Step 4: Update PR

1. Find the open PR for the current branch: `gh pr view --json number,body,title`
2. If no PR exists, skip this step and inform the user
3. Compare the current PR body against the new changes:
   - If the changes are within the existing PR scope, update the description to reflect the current state
   - If the changes are additive or a follow-up, add a PR comment summarizing what was just pushed instead
4. When updating the PR body, preserve the overall structure but refresh the summary bullets and test plan
5. When adding a comment, keep it concise — bullet points of what changed and why
6. **Before making any PR update (description edit or comment), show the user the exact text you plan to post and ask for their approval. Do NOT post until they confirm.**

## Rules

- Never commit files that look like secrets (.env, credentials, tokens)
- Never force push

gh pr create --draft --title "fix(clone): clean re-login hint + inline-login precondition" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

On an expired/absent session, `entire repo clone /gh/<owner>/<repo>` failed with the raw ogen-wrapped error chain, burying the one actionable line:

```
resolve mirror placements: security "BearerAuth": security source "BearerAuth": login session for "us.auth.entire.io" (https://us.auth.entire.io) expired; run `entire login` to re-authenticate
```

The `resolve mirror placements:` prefix and the generated `security "BearerAuth"` wrappers are noise; the friendly, context-named hint is already in the chain, just hidden.

## What changed

**Part 1 — clean message (every control-plane command).** `renderCoreError` (the shared choke point for org/project/repo/grant/mirror/clone) now detects the buried `*reauthError` via the new `auth.ReauthMessage` accessor and surfaces just its clean hint:

```
login session for "us.auth.entire.io" (https://us.auth.entire.io) expired; run `entire login` to re-authenticate
```

**Part 2 — `repo clone` inline-login precondition (active-context path).** Before the mirror lookup, clone probes the active session:
- **Interactive terminal:** prints the hint, then offers `Log in now and continue the clone?`. On yes it runs `entire login` in-process and continues in the same process (a fresh client re-reads the newly stored token). On no it exits with the clean hint.
- **Non-interactive (agents/CI):** prints the clean hint and exits non-zero — never blocks on a prompt.
- `--cluster` (different context) and a non-empty `ENTIRE_TOKEN` skip the precondition and rely on the Part 1 clean-message fallback.

`runLoginToServer` is factored out of the `login` command's `RunE` so the precondition reuses the exact login flow without duplication.

## Not doing

No central `main.go` catch or re-exec (that is #1794's `cli_upgrade_required` shape) — this is a scoped clone precondition instead.

## Testing

- `auth`: `TestReauthMessage` — both sentinels, deep-wrapped chain, non-reauth, nil.
- `cli`: `TestRenderCoreError_StripsReauthNoise` — clean message, no `resolve mirror placements` / `BearerAuth` noise.
- `cli`: `TestEnsureCloneSession` — healthy, non-TTY reauth (hint, no login), transient passthrough, `ENTIRE_TOKEN` skip, interactive login+continue, decline, login error.
- Full `cli` unit suite + `auth` tests green; `golangci-lint` 0 issues; `gofmt` clean.
- Not yet run locally: `mise run test:ci` (integration + canary) — CI will cover it; no hook/strategy paths touched.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

# Review PR Feedback

Walk every unresolved review thread on the PR for the current branch. For each
thread, decide whether it's actionable, fixable, or needs the user's input.
Apply fixes, post a reply explaining what changed, and resolve the thread.

## Step 1: Locate the PR

1. If `` is a number, use that PR.
2. Otherwise resolve from the current branch:
   ```
   gh pr view --json number,url
   ```
3. If there is no PR for the current branch, stop and tell the user.

## Step 2: List every review thread (resolved status + bodies)

GitHub's REST endpoints don't expose `isResolved`, so use GraphQL:

```
gh api graphql -f query='query {
  repository(owner:"<OWNER>", name:"<REPO>") {
    pullRequest(number:<NUM>) {
      reviewThreads(first:100) {
        nodes {
          id isResolved isOutdated path line
          comments(first:20) {
            nodes { databaseId author { login } body createdAt }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}'
```

Also pull issue-level comments for context:

```
gh api repos/<OWNER>/<REPO>/issues/<NUM>/comments
```

Save the GraphQL result so you can reference thread IDs and the first
comment's `databaseId` (used as the reply parent below).

## Step 3: Triage and group threads

For each thread that is **not** already `isResolved`:

- Read the body fully — bot comments (Cursor Bugbot, Copilot, etc.) are often
  long and the actionable bit is buried after metadata.
- Classify as one of:
  - **Easy fix** — uncontroversial, narrow scope (e.g. "use `f.Reader` instead
    of `f.Contents`", "add validation", "fix typo"). Just do it.
  - **Already fixed** — earlier commits on the branch already addressed the
    concern. Don't re-fix; reply explaining where it landed.
  - **Outdated/no longer applies** — code shape changed. Reply briefly noting
    the current state and resolve.
  - **Needs decision** — design tradeoff, scope question, or "won't fix"
    candidate. Hold for the user.
- For threads marked `isOutdated`: still address them; outdated ≠ irrelevant,
  GitHub just collapsed them because the underlying line moved.

Skip resolved threads silently — those have already been handled.

## Step 4: Ask the user about the hard ones

Before applying any fixes that involve a tradeoff or non-trivial scope, batch
the open questions into a single `AskUserQuestion` call. Group easy-fix
threads as one question ("OK to apply these N small fixes and resolve?"
with options for "do all", "do some", "skip"). Keep questions short and
include enough context that the user doesn't have to scroll back.

If a thread reports a security or correctness concern that needs a real
investigation (e.g. "race condition under concurrent X"), surface that
explicitly rather than treating it as easy.

## Step 5: Apply fixes

Make the code changes, then run before pushing:

```
go build ./...   # or the project's build command
mise run fmt
mise run lint
mise run test    # or test:ci, depending on scope
```

Fix any linter/test fallout from the changes. Don't push if anything is red.

If a `nolint` directive becomes "unused" after a config change, decide
between adding the type to the linter allowlist (preferred for stable cases)
or removing the directive — never both.

## Step 6: Commit and push

Stage only the files you changed (never `git add -A`). Use one commit per
logical group; e.g. one for the "easy fixes" batch, one per substantial
change. Commit messages focus on **why**, not **what**. Reference PR
threads by topic, not by GitHub numeric ID — those don't render anywhere
useful.

Push:

```
git push
```

## Step 7: Reply on each thread + resolve

Use the **first comment's `databaseId`** as the parent, not the thread ID:

```
# Reply
gh api -X POST "repos/<OWNER>/<REPO>/pulls/<NUM>/comments/<FIRST_COMMENT_DB_ID>/replies" \
  -f body="<reply text>"

# Resolve (thread ID is the GraphQL node id)
gh api graphql -f query='mutation($id: ID!) {
  resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: $id}) {
    thread { id isResolved }
  }
}' -F id="<THREAD_ID>"
```

Reply guidelines:

- Cite the commit hash that addressed the concern: `Fixed in abc1234.`
- Summarize **what** changed in one sentence — the reviewer doesn't need a
  detailed explanation, just enough to verify.
- For "won't fix" replies, give the rationale once, briefly. Don't argue.

## Step 8: Final sweep

After resolving everything you can, re-run the GraphQL query to confirm:

```
gh api graphql -f query='query { ... reviewThreads { nodes { id isResolved } } }'
```

Report to the user:
- Number of threads addressed (with one-line summary each)
- Number deferred and why
- Final commit hash + PR URL

## Rules

- Never resolve a thread without posting a reply first. The reply is the audit trail.
- Don't `--force` push.
- Don't bypass the build/lint/test gate to land "review fixes" — broken main is worse than slow review cycles.
- If a reviewer's concern is wrong, explain why in the reply and resolve. Don't leave open threads festering.
- If you genuinely can't tell what a thread is asking for, ask the user — don't guess and resolve.

Confirmed. That message is from `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/discovery.go` — printed by the **`git-remote-entire` helper** (a separate binary), not by our CLI. So two reasons, both scope-related:

**1. Full `entire://` URLs bypass the precondition entirely.** In clone's RunE the full-URL branch returns early to `runGitClone` *before* `ensureCloneSession`:
```go
if isEntireCloneURL(ref) {
    return runGitClone(...)   // ← your path exits here
}
...
if cluster == "" { ensureCloneSession(cmd) }   // ← never reached
```
Full URLs are pass-through to `git clone`, no lookup, no probe (by the approved plan's scope).

**2. Even the `/gh/` shorthand wouldn't prompt for this.** Our precondition probes the **active control-plane context**. The auth that actually failed here is **cluster STS in the helper** — `git clone` spawns `git-remote-entire`, which resolves a *cluster-specific* context for `aws-eu-central-1` via `clusterdiscovery`, prints its own hint, and aborts. Different binary, different context. We never gate it. If your active login were valid, the probe would pass and you'd still hit this helper error.

So the precondition guards the *lookup*, not the *clone*. Your test exercises the clone (helper) path, which we deliberately left on the static hint.

Fair — let me be straight about the gap between the intent and what's built.

## What we're actually doing right now
The precondition only fires on the **`/gh/` shorthand path with no `--cluster`**, and it checks your **active control-plane login**. Your full `entire://…` URL takes a different branch that returns early and shells straight to `git clone` — so it never reaches the precondition. That does **not** match "no matter the url." So on that point: you're right, it's inconsistent.

## But there's a deeper thing than "url form"
"Having a session" isn't one single thing. There are **two different auth scopes** in a clone:

1. **Active login** — what `entire login` gives you, what our probe checks.
2. **The target cluster's federation auth** — what the *actual clone* (STS) needs, resolved inside the `git-remote-entire` helper.

For a repo in your **own** federation these are the same. For a repo on **another** federation's cluster — exactly your case: repo on `aws-eu-central-1` while you're logged into `us` — they're **different**. Your error was scope #2 failing. A plain `entire login` to your active context would **not** have fixed that clone, because the clone needs a session for the `aws-eu-central-1` federation specifically.

So "require a session, else prompt" only truly works if we require the **right** session — the one the clone will actually use — not just any active login.

## What I think you actually want (and the correct design)
Make it a real, universal precondition on `entire repo clone`, for **every** URL form: before handing off to `git clone`, figure out the **target cluster** (from the `entire://` host, from `--cluster`, or from the chosen placement on the shorthand path) and ensure there's a usable session **for that cluster's federation** (reusing `ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster` → `clusterdiscovery`, the same resolver the helper uses). If missing/expired → prompt to log in to that federation → then continue.

That satisfies "no matter the url" *and* actually prevents the helper error you hit, instead of prompting for a session that wouldn't help.

- Does this two-scope picture match your mental model, or were you assuming a single account/session covers all clusters?
- Should I expand this PR to the cluster-aware precondition across all URL forms, or keep the PR as the message-cleanup + active-context prompt and do the cluster-aware work as a follow-up?

# Clean re-auth message + `repo clone` inline-login precondition

## Context

`entire repo clone /gh/entirehq/entire-records` on an expired session prints:

```
resolve mirror placements: security "BearerAuth": security source "BearerAuth": login session for "us.auth.entire.io" (https://us.auth.entire.io) expired; run `entire login` to re-authenticate
```

The actionable inner text is buried under two noise layers: `resolve mirror placements:` (`repo_clone.go:239`) and the generated ogen wrappers `security "BearerAuth": security source "BearerAuth":` (`internal/coreapi/oas_*.go`, not editable). The friendly text originates from `*reauthError` (`auth/refresh.go:139-174`), which is preserved intact in the chain and unwraps to `tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired` / `ErrNotLoggedIn`.

Two improvements (user-approved):
1. **All control-plane commands** — strip the noise, show only the clean re-login hint.
2. **`repo clone`** — treat a usable session as a precondition: if missing/expired and the terminal is interactive, offer to run `entire login` inline and continue the clone in the same process; otherwise fall back to the clean hint.

Not doing: a central main.go catch or re-exec (that's PR #1794's `cli_upgrade_required` shape — deliberately not reused here). This work is unrelated to the current `fix/local-repo-checkpoint-probe` branch and should land as its own PR branched off `main`.

## Part 1 — clean re-auth message (base, fixes every control-plane command)

All control-plane commands funnel errors through `renderCoreError` (`cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go:639`) via `runCore`→`runCoreClient`. It only recognizes RFC-7807 (`coreapi.APIError`) and passes auth errors through raw.

**New accessor in the auth package** — `cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go`, beside `reauthError`:

```go
// ReauthMessage returns the friendly, context-named re-login message carried by
// a *reauthError anywhere in err's chain, ok=false otherwise. Cross-package
// accessor for the unexported type — the cli package can't errors.As it, and
// string-matching the top-level message is wrong (two noise layers wrap it).
func ReauthMessage(err error) (string, bool) {

## Goal (user's exact UX requirement)
`entire repo clone` must NEVER fail for lack of a usable session. This must hold for all three URL forms.

1. `entire repo clone` RunE in `cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go` has three paths:
   - (a) full `entire://<cluster>/gh/<owner>/<repo>` URL → early return `runGitClone(ctx, cmd, ref, targetDir)` at ~line 120-122 (currently forwarded verbatim, NOT validated).
   - (b) `/gh/` shorthand + `--cluster` → placements lookup via `runCoreForCluster(cmd, cluster, ...)`, then `selectCloneTarget`.
   - (c) `/gh/` shorthand, no `--cluster` → placements lookup via active-context `runCore`, then `selectCloneTarget` → `chosen.ClusterHost`.
   The target cluster host is known: (a) by parsing the URL; (b) from the `--cluster` flag (validated at ~line 161); (c) only AFTER `selectCloneTarget` returns `chosen.ClusterHost` (~line 176-188). Then `mirrorCloneURL(host,owner,repo)` → `runGitClone`.

2. The clone's actual auth: `git clone` execs `git-remote-entire` (`cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go`), which calls `clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterAuth(ctx, cfgDir, cacheDir, host, ...)` → picks a local context whose `CoreURL` (JWT `iss`) ∈ the cluster's advertised `core_urls`, then uses its login JWT as the bearer. 3. A context becomes eligible by `entire login --server <X>` where `<X>` is origin-equal to one of the cluster's `core_urls` (because `CoreURL == iss == --server origin`, enforced at login).

4. File: internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/resolve.go (ResolveClusterCores ~line 123), internal/entireclient/discovery/cluster_cores.go. `discovery.Discover(ctx, host, httpClient, debugf)` is the uncached direct fetch.

5. `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster(ctx, clusterHost)` (cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go:81) resolves the eligible context for a cluster and returns `ControlPlaneTarget{CoreURL, TokenSource}` — the SAME resolver the helper uses, so calling it + `TokenSource(ctx)` accurately predicts helper success. 7. **Test plan**: unit/command tests for each branch using seams (no real network/TTY), following repo rules (t.Parallel only where seams aren't swapped; ENTIRE_TEST_TTY; config isolation). Reference repo_clone_test.go and repo_clone_login_test.go.

## Context

Original goal (PR #1931, draft, already on branch `fix/clone-reauth-hint`): stop `entire repo clone` from dumping the noisy ogen-wrapped auth chain, and prompt to log in. What shipped so far:
- **Part 1** — `auth.ReauthMessage` + `renderCoreError`/`runCoreClient` clean the re-auth message for every control-plane command.
- **Part 2** — an **active-context** clone precondition (`ensureCloneSession`) that prompts inline login on the `/gh/` shorthand path.

Gap the user hit while testing `entire repo clone entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/...`:
```
fatal: no auth context for cluster aws-eu-central-1.entire.io.
Log in with `entire login`, then re-run your command.
```
Two reasons: (1) the full-`entire://` path returns early to `git clone`, bypassing the precondition; (2) the precondition only checks the **active control-plane login**, but the clone's real auth is **cluster-scoped** — `git-remote-entire` needs a local context whose `CoreURL` (JWT `iss`) is in the **target cluster's** advertised `core_urls`. Logging into the active/default region does not help when the repo lives in another region's federation.

**Requirement:** `entire repo clone` must never fail for lack of a usable session — ensure a session eligible for the **target cluster** before `git clone`, and if missing, log the user into the **correct region** (one of that cluster's `core_urls`) in-process, then continue. "no auth context for cluster" = **zero eligible contexts**. The helper owns git's stdout and cannot prompt. - `ErrAmbiguousContext` — wrap the `default` return (resolve.go:248).
Discovery errors stay untyped (they fall into the cli "else" branch). Existing `resolve_test.go` assertions keep passing (text unchanged); add coverage that the new sentinels match.

## Step 2 — `auth` helpers (`cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go`)

- `ClusterLoginServers(ctx, clusterHost) ([]string, error)` → `clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterCores(ctx, userdirs.Cache(), host, &http.Client{Timeout: controlPlaneClusterDiscoveryTimeout}, nil)` then return `entry.CoreURLs`. var (

    interactiveClusterLogin  = defaultInteractiveClusterLogin   // func(cmd, servers []string, hint string) (bool, error)

- **Manual**: with no context eligible for `aws-eu-central-1`, `entire repo clone entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/gtrrz-victor/testing-rift` in a real terminal → offers login to the cluster's region → clone continues; piped/non-TTY → clean hint naming the region, exit 1.

Not doing: a central main.go catch or re-exec (that's PR #1794's `cli_upgrade_required` shape — deliberately not reused here). This work is unrelated to the current `fix/local-repo-checkpoint-probe` branch and should land as its own PR branched off `main`.

// accessor for the unexported type — the cli package can't errors.As it, and
// string-matching the top-level message is wrong (two noise layers wrap it).
func ReauthMessage(err error) (string, bool) {
	var re *reauthError
	if errors.As(err, &re) {
		return re.Error(), true
	}
	return "", false
}
```

# `entire repo clone` — never fail for a missing session; log in to the correct region

## Context

Original goal (PR #1931, draft, already on branch `fix/clone-reauth-hint`): stop `entire repo clone` from dumping the noisy ogen-wrapped auth chain, and prompt to log in. What shipped so far:
- **Part 1** — `auth.ReauthMessage` + `renderCoreError`/`runCoreClient` clean the re-auth message for every control-plane command.
- **Part 2** — an **active-context** clone precondition (`ensureCloneSession`) that prompts inline login on the `/gh/` shorthand path.

Gap the user hit while testing `entire repo clone entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/...`:
```
fatal: no auth context for cluster aws-eu-central-1.entire.io.
Log in with `entire login`, then re-run your command.
```
Two reasons: (1) the full-`entire://` path returns early to `git clone`, bypassing the precondition; (2) the precondition only checks the **active control-plane login**, but the clone's real auth is **cluster-scoped** — `git-remote-entire` needs a local context whose `CoreURL` (JWT `iss`) is in the **target cluster's** advertised `core_urls`. Logging into the active/default region does not help when the repo lives in another region's federation.

**Requirement:** `entire repo clone` must never fail for lack of a usable session — ensure a session eligible for the **target cluster** before `git clone`, and if missing, log the user into the **correct region** (one of that cluster's `core_urls`) in-process, then continue. Applies to all three URL forms.

## How the clone actually authenticates (verified)
`git clone entire://<cluster>/...` execs `git-remote-entire`, which calls `clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterAuth(host)` → picks a local context whose `CoreURL` ∈ the cluster's `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` `core_urls`, and uses its login JWT as the bearer. "no auth context for cluster" = **zero eligible contexts**. The helper owns git's stdout and cannot prompt. The fix is `entire login --server <X>` where `X` ∈ that cluster's `core_urls` (`CoreURL == iss == --server origin`). `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster(ctx, host)` uses the **same resolver**, so probing it + `TokenSource(ctx)` predicts helper success and (on success) warms `cluster_cores.json`.

## Step 1 — Typed classification sentinels (`internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/resolve.go`)
The failure modes from `selectContext` are untyped plain strings today (no-eligible via `renderLoginHint`, ambiguous via `ambiguousContextError`, discovery via `formatDiscoveryError`). Add two exported sentinels and make the two eligibility errors `errors.Is`-match them **without changing their rendered text** (tiny typed error with an `Is`/`Unwrap`):
- `ErrNoEligibleContext` — wrap the `case 0` return (resolve.go:243).
- `ErrAmbiguousContext` — wrap the `default` return (resolve.go:248).
Discovery errors stay untyped (they fall into the cli "else" branch). Existing `resolve_test.go` assertions keep passing (text unchanged); add coverage that the new sentinels match.

## Step 2 — `auth` helpers (`cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go`)
`auth` already imports `clusterdiscovery`; cli must not (keeps layering — cli imports `clusterdiscovery` only in tests today).
- `ClusterLoginServers(ctx, clusterHost) ([]string, error)` → `clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterCores(ctx, userdirs.Cache(), host, &http.Client{Timeout: controlPlaneClusterDiscoveryTimeout}, nil)` then return `entry.CoreURLs`. Cache-first (warmed by the probe above → no second network call in the common path).
- Re-export the sentinels: `var ErrNoEligibleContext = clusterdiscovery.ErrNoEligibleContext`, `var ErrAmbiguousContext = clusterdiscovery.ErrAmbiguousContext`.

## Step 3 — Cluster-aware precondition + seams (`cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go`)
New package-level seams (mirroring the existing `probeCloneSession`/`interactiveReauthLogin` pair so tests stub without network/keychain/TTY):
```
var (
    probeClusterCloneSession = defaultProbeClusterCloneSession  // func(ctx, host) (servers []string, err error)
    interactiveClusterLogin  = defaultInteractiveClusterLogin   // func(cmd, servers []string, hint string) (bool, error)
)
```
`defaultProbeClusterCloneSession(ctx, host)`:
1. `target, err := auth.ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster(ctx, host)`.
2. `err == nil`: mint `target.TokenSource(ctx)` → nil error ⇒ `return nil, nil` (usable); reauth/transient ⇒ `return []string{target.CoreURL}, terr`.
3. `errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNoEligibleContext)`: `servers, cerr := auth.ClusterLoginServers(ctx, host)`; `return servers, err` (err keeps the sentinel; servers = login targets).
4. else (ambiguous / discovery / transient): `return nil, err`.

`ensureClusterCloneSession(cmd, clusterHost)`:
- Skip on `os.LookupEnv(auth.EnvTokenVar)` presence (helper validates env bearer itself; matches existing `ensureCloneSession`).
- `if insecureHTTPRequested(cmd) { auth.EnableInsecureHTTP() }`.
- `servers, probeErr := probeClusterCloneSession(...)`; nil ⇒ return nil.
- Classify `probeErr`:
  - `auth.ReauthMessage` matches (expired single context) → hint = that message, servers = `[target.CoreURL]`.
  - `errors.Is(probeErr, auth.ErrNoEligibleContext)` → hint names `servers` (see messages).
  - `errors.Is(probeErr, auth.ErrAmbiguousContext)` → return `probeErr` verbatim (says "run `entire auth use`"); **never auto-login** (user already has valid contexts).
  - else (discovery/transient) → return `probeErr` verbatim (`formatDiscoveryError` is already friendly); never prompt.
  - For the two promptable cases: non-interactive → `errors.New(hint)`; interactive → `interactiveClusterLogin(cmd, servers, hint)`; declined → `NewSilentError(errors.New(hint))` (hint already printed); login error → propagate.

`defaultInteractiveClusterLogin(cmd, servers, hint)` — generalizes the existing `defaultInteractiveReauthLogin` into one implementation (single-server callers pass a 1-element slice):
- honor `ctx.Err()`; print `hint` to stderr.
- `len(servers) > 1` → `NewAccessibleForm` + `huh.NewSelect[string]()` "Pick the region to log in to for `<host>`:" → `server`; else `server = servers[0]`.
- `huh.NewConfirm().Title("Log in now and continue the clone?")` (abort/cancel handling as in `confirmControlPlaneDeletion`).
- confirm → `runLoginToServer(ctx, out, err, server, insecureHTTPRequested(cmd), false)` → true.

Refactor: fold `defaultInteractiveReauthLogin` into `defaultInteractiveClusterLogin` (keeps `TestEnsureCloneSession` assertions valid).

- **Full `entire://` URL** (currently early-returns at ~L120): `if host,_,_,_,perr := parseMirrorCloneURL(ref); perr == nil { ensureClusterCloneSession(cmd, host) }` then `runGitClone`. If parse fails, keep today's verbatim forward (don't newly reject a URL git might handle).
- **`--cluster`**: after `validateClusterHost(cluster)` and before `runWithCore`, `ensureClusterCloneSession(cmd, cluster)` (covers both the `runCoreForCluster` lookup and the clone).
- **Shorthand, no `--cluster`**: keep `ensureCloneSession(cmd)` before the active-context placements lookup (distinct auth stage), then after `selectCloneTarget` + `validateClusterHost(chosen.ClusterHost)` and before `runGitClone`, `ensureClusterCloneSession(cmd, chosen.ClusterHost)` (silent when the chosen cluster shares the active federation).

## Step 5 — Messages
- **No-eligible** (implements the discovery.go:153 TODO, composed in cli where `servers` is held): `no auth context for cluster <host>.` + `Log in to one of its regions: entire login --server <core1>` (list the rest). Interactive: print, then confirm (or Select for multi-core).
- **Expired**: reuse `auth.ReauthMessage` text + confirm.
- **Ambiguous**: verbatim `ambiguousContextError` (names contexts + `entire auth use`).
- **Discovery/network**: verbatim `formatDiscoveryError` ("doesn't look like a cluster, or it is unreachable", etc.).

## Critical files
- `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/resolve.go` — two sentinels (Step 1).
- `cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go` — `ClusterLoginServers` + sentinel re-exports (Step 2).
- `cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go` — precondition, seams, RunE wiring (Steps 3–4).
- Reuse: `parseMirrorCloneURL` (repo_mirror.go:1263), `runLoginToServer` (login.go:101), `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster` (control_plane.go:81), `clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterCores` (resolve.go:123), `NewAccessibleForm`/`confirmControlPlaneDeletion` pattern, `NewSilentError`, `insecureHTTPRequested`, `validateClusterHost`, `userdirs.Cache()`.

## Verification / tests
- **clusterdiscovery**: sentinels `errors.Is`-match at the 0 and >1 branches; rendered text byte-identical (existing `resolve_test.go` stays green).
- **cli** — new `repo_clone_cluster_login_test.go` (non-parallel; swaps seams), patterned on `repo_clone_login_test.go`. Cover `ensureClusterCloneSession` branches: usable→no prompt; expired-single→`interactiveClusterLogin` gets `[CoreURL]`; no-eligible non-interactive→hint lists cores; no-eligible interactive single/multi core→login (Select for multi); ambiguous→surfaced, login never called; discovery error→surfaced; `ENTIRE_TOKEN` present/empty→probe skipped. Reuse `unsetCloneEnvToken`, `interactive.EnvTestTTY`, and the `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR=t.TempDir()` idiom to mint a real `*reauthError`.

- `mise run fmt && mise run lint` (0 issues) + `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... ./internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/...`.
- **Manual**: with no context eligible for `aws-eu-central-1`, `entire repo clone entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/gtrrz-victor/testing-rift` in a real terminal → offers login to the cluster's region → clone continues; piped/non-TTY → clean hint naming the region, exit 1.

## Risks
1. **Sentinels are a hard prerequisite** for clean classification (vs fragile string-matching localized text). Small: 2 call sites, text preserved.
2. **Ambiguous case is intentionally not auto-logged-in** — user has valid contexts; the fix is `entire auth use`.
3. **`ResolveClusterCores` uses requireAudience=true** — may refetch/fail on an audience-less cluster; harmless (such clusters aren't clonable).
4. **Full-URL path gains a network probe + validation** before `git clone` (behavior change from verbatim-forward), scoped to parseable `entire://…/gh/…` refs; unparseable refs still forward untouched.
5. Lands on the existing draft PR #1931 (same goal); the clusterdiscovery sentinel change is small and tightly coupled, not a separable concern.

# `entire repo clone` — never fail for a missing session; log in to the correct region

## Context

Original goal (PR #1931, draft, already on branch `fix/clone-reauth-hint`): stop `entire repo clone` from dumping the noisy ogen-wrapped auth chain, and prompt to log in. What shipped so far:
- **Part 1** — `auth.ReauthMessage` + `renderCoreError`/`runCoreClient` clean the re-auth message for every control-plane command.
- **Part 2** — an **active-context** clone precondition (`ensureCloneSession`) that prompts inline login on the `/gh/` shorthand path.

Gap the user hit while testing `entire repo clone entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/...`:
```
fatal: no auth context for cluster aws-eu-central-1.entire.io.
Log in with `entire login`, then re-run your command.
```
Two reasons: (1) the full-`entire://` path returns early to `git clone`, bypassing the precondition; (2) the precondition only checks the **active control-plane login**, but the clone's real auth is **cluster-scoped** — `git-remote-entire` needs a local context whose `CoreURL` (JWT `iss`) is in the **target cluster's** advertised `core_urls`. Logging into the active/default region does not help when the repo lives in another region's federation.

**Requirement:** `entire repo clone` must never fail for lack of a usable session — ensure a session eligible for the **target cluster** before `git clone`, and if missing, log the user into the **correct region** (one of that cluster's `core_urls`) in-process, then continue. Applies to all three URL forms.

## How the clone actually authenticates (verified)
`git clone entire://<cluster>/...` execs `git-remote-entire`, which calls `clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterAuth(host)` → picks a local context whose `CoreURL` ∈ the cluster's `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` `core_urls`, and uses its login JWT as the bearer. "no auth context for cluster" = **zero eligible contexts**. The helper owns git's stdout and cannot prompt. The fix is `entire login --server <X>` where `X` ∈ that cluster's `core_urls` (`CoreURL == iss == --server origin`). `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster(ctx, host)` uses the **same resolver**, so probing it + `TokenSource(ctx)` predicts helper success and (on success) warms `cluster_cores.json`.

## Step 1 — Typed classification sentinels (`internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/resolve.go`)
The failure modes from `selectContext` are untyped plain strings today (no-eligible via `renderLoginHint`, ambiguous via `ambiguousContextError`, discovery via `formatDiscoveryError`). Add two exported sentinels and make the two eligibility errors `errors.Is`-match them **without changing their rendered text** (tiny typed error with an `Is`/`Unwrap`):
- `ErrNoEligibleContext` — wrap the `case 0` return (resolve.go:243).
- `ErrAmbiguousContext` — wrap the `default` return (resolve.go:248).
Discovery errors stay untyped (they fall into the cli "else" branch). Existing `resolve_test.go` assertions keep passing (text unchanged); add coverage that the new sentinels match.

## Step 2 — `auth` helpers (`cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go`)
`auth` already imports `clusterdiscovery`; cli must not (keeps layering — cli imports `clusterdiscovery` only in tests today).
- `ClusterLoginServers(ctx, clusterHost) ([]string, error)` → `clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterCores(ctx, userdirs.Cache(), host, &http.Client{Timeout: controlPlaneClusterDiscoveryTimeout}, nil)` then return `entry.CoreURLs`. Cache-first (warmed by the probe above → no second network call in the common path).
- Re-export the sentinels: `var ErrNoEligibleContext = clusterdiscovery.ErrNoEligibleContext`, `var ErrAmbiguousContext = clusterdiscovery.ErrAmbiguousContext`.

## Step 3 — Cluster-aware precondition + seams (`cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go`)
New package-level seams (mirroring the existing `probeCloneSession`/`interactiveReauthLogin` pair so tests stub without network/keychain/TTY):
```
var (
    probeClusterCloneSession = defaultProbeClusterCloneSession  // func(ctx, host) (servers []string, err error)
    interactiveClusterLogin  = defaultInteractiveClusterLogin   // func(cmd, servers []string, hint string) (bool, error)
)
```
`defaultProbeClusterCloneSession(ctx, host)`:
1. `target, err := auth.ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster(ctx, host)`.
2. `err == nil`: mint `target.TokenSource(ctx)` → nil error ⇒ `return nil, nil` (usable); reauth/transient ⇒ `return []string{target.CoreURL}, terr`.
3. `errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNoEligibleContext)`: `servers, cerr := auth.ClusterLoginServers(ctx, host)`; `return servers, err` (err keeps the sentinel; servers = login targets).
4. else (ambiguous / discovery / transient): `return nil, err`.

`ensureClusterCloneSession(cmd, clusterHost)`:
- Skip on `os.LookupEnv(auth.EnvTokenVar)` presence (helper validates env bearer itself; matches existing `ensureCloneSession`).
- `if insecureHTTPRequested(cmd) { auth.EnableInsecureHTTP() }`.
- `servers, probeErr := probeClusterCloneSession(...)`; nil ⇒ return nil.
- Classify `probeErr`:
  - `auth.ReauthMessage` matches (expired single context) → hint = that message, servers = `[target.CoreURL]`.
  - `errors.Is(probeErr, auth.ErrNoEligibleContext)` → hint names `servers` (see messages).
  - `errors.Is(probeErr, auth.ErrAmbiguousContext)` → return `probeErr` verbatim (says "run `entire auth use`"); **never auto-login** (user already has valid contexts).
  - else (discovery/transient) → return `probeErr` verbatim (`formatDiscoveryError` is already friendly); never prompt.
  - For the two promptable cases: non-interactive → `errors.New(hint)`; interactive → `interactiveClusterLogin(cmd, servers, hint)`; declined → `NewSilentError(errors.New(hint))` (hint already printed); login error → propagate.

`defaultInteractiveClusterLogin(cmd, servers, hint)` — generalizes the existing `defaultInteractiveReauthLogin` into one implementation (single-server callers pass a 1-element slice):
- honor `ctx.Err()`; print `hint` to stderr.
- `len(servers) > 1` → `NewAccessibleForm` + `huh.NewSelect[string]()` "Pick the region to log in to for `<host>`:" → `server`; else `server = servers[0]`.
- `huh.NewConfirm().Title("Log in now and continue the clone?")` (abort/cancel handling as in `confirmControlPlaneDeletion`).
- confirm → `runLoginToServer(ctx, out, err, server, insecureHTTPRequested(cmd), false)` → true.

Refactor: fold `defaultInteractiveReauthLogin` into `defaultInteractiveClusterLogin` (keeps `TestEnsureCloneSession` assertions valid).

## Step 4 — Wire into all three RunE paths (`repo_clone.go`)
- **Full `entire://` URL** (currently early-returns at ~L120): `if host,_,_,_,perr := parseMirrorCloneURL(ref); perr == nil { ensureClusterCloneSession(cmd, host) }` then `runGitClone`. If parse fails, keep today's verbatim forward (don't newly reject a URL git might handle).
- **`--cluster`**: after `validateClusterHost(cluster)` and before `runWithCore`, `ensureClusterCloneSession(cmd, cluster)` (covers both the `runCoreForCluster` lookup and the clone).
- **Shorthand, no `--cluster`**: keep `ensureCloneSession(cmd)` before the active-context placements lookup (distinct auth stage), then after `selectCloneTarget` + `validateClusterHost(chosen.ClusterHost)` and before `runGitClone`, `ensureClusterCloneSession(cmd, chosen.ClusterHost)` (silent when the chosen cluster shares the active federation).

## Step 5 — Messages
- **No-eligible** (implements the discovery.go:153 TODO, composed in cli where `servers` is held): `no auth context for cluster <host>.` + `Log in to one of its regions: entire login --server <core1>` (list the rest). Interactive: print, then confirm (or Select for multi-core).
- **Expired**: reuse `auth.ReauthMessage` text + confirm.
- **Ambiguous**: verbatim `ambiguousContextError` (names contexts + `entire auth use`).
- **Discovery/network**: verbatim `formatDiscoveryError` ("doesn't look like a cluster, or it is unreachable", etc.).

## Critical files
- `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/resolve.go` — two sentinels (Step 1).
- `cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go` — `ClusterLoginServers` + sentinel re-exports (Step 2).
- `cmd/entire/cli/repo_clone.go` — precondition, seams, RunE wiring (Steps 3–4).
- Reuse: `parseMirrorCloneURL` (repo_mirror.go:1263), `runLoginToServer` (login.go:101), `auth.ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster` (control_plane.go:81), `clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterCores` (resolve.go:123), `NewAccessibleForm`/`confirmControlPlaneDeletion` pattern, `NewSilentError`, `insecureHTTPRequested`, `validateClusterHost`, `userdirs.Cache()`.

## Verification / tests
- **clusterdiscovery**: sentinels `errors.Is`-match at the 0 and >1 branches; rendered text byte-identical (existing `resolve_test.go` stays green).
- **cli** — new `repo_clone_cluster_login_test.go` (non-parallel; swaps seams), patterned on `repo_clone_login_test.go`. Cover `ensureClusterCloneSession` branches: usable→no prompt; expired-single→`interactiveClusterLogin` gets `[CoreURL]`; no-eligible non-interactive→hint lists cores; no-eligible interactive single/multi core→login (Select for multi); ambiguous→surfaced, login never called; discovery error→surfaced; `ENTIRE_TOKEN` present/empty→probe skipped. Reuse `unsetCloneEnvToken`, `interactive.EnvTestTTY`, and the `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR=t.TempDir()` idiom to mint a real `*reauthError`.
- **RunE wiring** (extend `repo_clone_test.go`): swap `probeClusterCloneSession` to record the host; assert full-URL forwards the parsed host, unparseable `entire://` skips the precondition, `--cluster` forwards the flag host, shorthand forwards `chosen.ClusterHost`.
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint` (0 issues) + `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... ./internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/...`.
- **Manual**: with no context eligible for `aws-eu-central-1`, `entire repo clone entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/gtrrz-victor/testing-rift` in a real terminal → offers login to the cluster's region → clone continues; piped/non-TTY → clean hint naming the region, exit 1.

## Risks
1. **Sentinels are a hard prerequisite** for clean classification (vs fragile string-matching localized text). Small: 2 call sites, text preserved.
2. **Ambiguous case is intentionally not auto-logged-in** — user has valid contexts; the fix is `entire auth use`.
3. **`ResolveClusterCores` uses requireAudience=true** — may refetch/fail on an audience-less cluster; harmless (such clusters aren't clonable).
4. **Full-URL path gains a network probe + validation** before `git clone` (behavior change from verbatim-forward), scoped to parseable `entire://…/gh/…` refs; unparseable refs still forward untouched.
5. Lands on the existing draft PR #1931 (same goal); the clusterdiscovery sentinel change is small and tightly coupled, not a separable concern.

content.text:
Pushed as `5889ca44f`. The PR scope grew a lot (from message-cleanup to cluster-aware region login), so the description needs a rewrite. Here's what I'd post to PR #1931 — I won't push it until you approve:

---

**Title:** `fix(clone): never fail on a missing session — log in to the correct region`

**Body:**

## Problem
`entire repo clone` failed hard when the caller lacked a usable session. Two shapes:
- Any control-plane path dumped the raw ogen-wrapped chain (`resolve mirror placements: security "BearerAuth": … expired; run entire login`).
- A repo on **another region's cluster** failed with `fatal: no auth context for cluster <host>` from `git-remote-entire` (which can't prompt), because clone auth is **cluster-scoped** — the helper needs a local context whose `CoreURL` is in the target cluster's advertised `core_urls`, not just any active login.

## What changed
1. **Clean re-auth message (every control-plane command).** `auth.ReauthMessage` + `renderCoreError`/`runCoreClient` surface only the actionable `run entire login` hint.
2. **Active-context precondition** for the `/gh/` placements lookup: prompt inline login when interactive, clean hint + non-zero exit otherwise.
3. **Cluster-aware precondition** (the fix for the cross-region case), wired into all three URL forms — full `entire://`, `--cluster`, and shorthand after placement selection. Probes the **target cluster** via `ResolveControlPlaneTargetForCluster`; when no eligible session exists, offers to `entire login --server <core>` for that cluster's region (a picker when several cores are trusted) and continues in-process. Non-interactive → clean hint naming the region. Ambiguous-context (`entire auth use`) and discovery failures are surfaced verbatim. Adds `clusterdiscovery.ErrNoEligibleContext`/`ErrAmbiguousContext` sentinels for clean classification.

## Not doing
No central main.go catch / re-exec (that's #1794's `cli_upgrade_required` shape). `ENTIRE_TOKEN` runs skip the precondition (helper validates the bearer itself).

## Testing
`ReauthMessage`, `renderCoreError` noise-strip, `ensureCloneSession` (7 cases), `ensureClusterCloneSession` (11 cases: usable / expired / no-eligible ×TTY×single/multi / ambiguous / discovery / decline / login-error / env-token), RunE wiring (full-URL + `--cluster` forward the right host), clusterdiscovery sentinels. Full `cli` + `auth` + `clusterdiscovery` suites, `golangci-lint`, `gofmt` all green. Manual: cross-region `entire://` clone offers region login → continues; piped → clean hint, exit 1.

On inferring the cluster from the clone URL — depends which URL shape:

**Full `entire://<cluster>/gh/owner/repo`** — cluster is *in* the URL. We already infer it: `parseMirrorCloneURL(ref)` → host → probe that cluster directly. Your working test hits exactly this: no active-context login needed, we go straight to the target-cluster precondition.

**Shorthand `/gh/owner/repo`** — no cluster in the ref. A repo can be mirrored on 0/1/many clusters, so we can't infer it from the string. We resolve owner/repo → cluster(s) via the pull-gated `/mirrors/placements` API (needs the active control-plane login), then pick `chosen.ClusterHost`. The lookup *is* the inference, and it requires auth — that's why the shorthand path keeps the active-context precondition before the cluster one.

So: for `entire://` and `--cluster` we already derive the cluster and require only that cluster's session. The only case that can't be inferred from the URL alone is the bare `/gh/` shorthand.

Which did you mean? If it's the shorthand — wanting to skip the active-context login and jump straight to the target cluster — that's not cleanly possible: nothing but the authenticated placements call maps `owner/repo` → cluster. If you meant the `entire://` case, we're already doing it.
